reported_performance: Long-running facility instrument; a major 2026 detector/fibre/pipeline upgrade introduced an offset requiring continuity calibration
Solar and stellar time series demonstrate sub-m/s analysis capability, but the achieved scatter remains target- and pipeline-dependent
On-sky instrument paper reports mode-dependent performance; design and calibration terms must not be conflated with stellar RV scatter
Instrument calibration precision below 0.10 m/s was reported, explicitly excluding photon noise and stellar variability
Official commissioning material reports quiet-star variability below 1 m/s and a tau Ceti sequence below 0.5 m/s; this is not a universal floor
Short-term performance exceeded a 0.5 m/s target, but current long-term interpretation is limited by detector thermal events and a 2026 vacuum-pump failure
Dual VIS/NIR channels enable chromatic activity diagnosis; channel resolutions and RV information content differ
Cryogenic NIR design targets M dwarfs; published performance depends strongly on telluric masking, calibration, and stellar type
Combines NIR velocimetry and spectropolarimetry, supporting direct activity diagnostics rather than RV precision alone
Operational since April 2023 with public pipeline-reduced spectra; high-accuracy mode is designed around approximately 1 m/s capability
Regular visiting-instrument use has demonstrated sub-m/s short-term RV performance on selected targets
Delivered in October 2025; installation and commissioning continue through 2026 for the Terra Hunting Experiment
Baseline wavelength precision is 1 m/s with a 0.1 m/s goal; these are requirements, not achieved performance
